scope: Step 1 of native redesign: bounded IEEE smoke test, then supported QFloat alternatives on real-weight isolated depthwise layers. No production executor/library/native image or historical numerical policy changed.

ieee.observed: IEEE FP32 multiply/add, FP16-input FP32 multiply-accumulate, and FP16 accumulation return all-zero destinations on distinct finite dyadic fixtures. FP32/FP16 input echoes and QFloat arithmetic controls pass.
ieee.interpretation: Consistent with optional IEEE extension unavailable in the present core/platform configuration. Hardware absence versus platform disablement is not established. Compiler support alone does not prove silicon availability.

modes.0: Original QFloat multiply, convert to FP32, checked multiply, add with zero-identity preservation and convert each tap.
modes.1: FP32 operands, persistent QFloat32 accumulation; convert once after all taps. Changes rounding schedule and zero handling.
modes.2: FP16 operands, QFloat32 pair products/accumulation; convert once after all taps. Actual mixed IEEE FP32 FMA is not used.

method.corpus: Four hash-pinned recorded crops; actual ncnn layer inputs and model weights; all channels of four representative depthwise layers.
method.geometry: 112-wide stride one, 112-to-56 stride two, 14-wide and 7-wide stride one. Native images specialize the known geometry and validate it against the descriptor.
method.timing: Native row brackets separately measure staging, gather+arithmetic, store/check and total kernel body. VTCM counters and specialized geometry reduce probe register pressure; no vector job-stack accesses. Full wrapper, audited host submission and host pad/convert preparation remain separately reported. Gather and arithmetic are deliberately a combined scope, not separately inferred.
method.data: Host-created padded panels live in the borrowed 128 KiB job arena. Native staging, coefficient preparation and outputs use only the saved 8 KiB VTCM. No resident graph tensors are accessed. No cached data alias, persistent tensor layout or producer-consumer fusion is implemented.
method.accuracy: Local ordered FP32 reference, precision-matched local reference and pinned ncnn output compared separately. A conservative term-magnitude arithmetic bound rejects gross corruption; it is not a tracking-quality threshold. Finite/normal-coefficient and absolute intermediate range proofs run before submission; native input/preclip finite flags remain enabled.
method.checks: Worker/SSR/EVB, code-PC/fault location, existing 40ms wrapper limit, cache cleanup and per-job restoration before acknowledgment. Numerical comparisons follow completed restoration so an oracle mismatch can stop cleanly. Native row checkpoints enforce the existing 20ms local budget; partial completion is refused without retry.

development.initial_numeric_stop: The initial IEEE oracle rejected an all-zero mixed result after its audited restoration had completed. No native fault or poison. A read-only full arena/health comparison against the failed-run pre-snapshot passed before diagnostic captures; QFloat worked while every IEEE variant zeroed.
development.generic_pilot: Earlier generic kernels passed on the calibration crop. Their timings are superseded by the source-pinned geometry-specialized/VTCM-counter matrix; no failed or generic timing sample enters the final layer table.

conclusion: Precision relaxation is usable through supported QFloat instructions, but these isolated kernels show modest body-time gains only: about 1.2x on large maps and 1.03x on small maps for half storage. Deferred FP32-input conversion alone gains at most a few percent of total body time here. Stage/other work dominates. IEEE-specific arithmetic cannot be used in the present configuration.
next: Prototype channel-blocked depthwise tiles that fill vector lanes and reuse staged rows/coefficient tiles in VTCM. Compare equal layouts/tiling with FP32 and FP16 storage, retaining QFloat32 reduction, before deciding precision. Convolution/HMX staging and fusion still require redesign to approach 17-25ms native per crop.
limitations: Isolated padded/staged CHW kernels, not the optimized resident row-tiling executor. Ratios compare arithmetic variants of the SAME probe, not a speedup of the current graph.
Total body includes prototype staging/coefficient/bookkeeping costs and instrumentation; scalar stack accesses remain. Component timings describe this probe schedule, not a hardware execution floor.
One pass per crop/mode, three register-slope samples per count, one boot; no randomized repeated layer timing or sustained thermal qualification.

Half inputs add local max deviation up to 0.0289793 versus FP32/ncnn on these crops; matched-precision arithmetic error is much smaller. No task-level acceptance threshold, whole-graph four-head accuracy or tracking validation is established.

All four crops share one recording/scene. Padding/quantization preparation and repeated cached job publication are outside kernel body and separately measured; results are not end-to-end frame latency.
